notes: The documented full grammar is a literal include derived directly from Grammar/python.gram, but omits CPython code generation and error recovery details.
Rules whose names start with invalid_ are second-pass parser rules used for specialized SyntaxError behavior and are not part of ordinary first-pass parsing.

grammar_boundaries.description: The full grammar target is pinned to the CPython 3.14.6 PEG grammar and docs hash recorded in this profile.

The current executable frontend uses CPython ast.parse as a parser oracle for supported file, interactive, and eval inputs, then lowers supported AST constructs to K while preserving construct identity for the current adapter subset.

A native K frontend or formally specified parser frontend must cover the full token stream, PEG operators, soft keywords, invalid_* second-pass diagnostics, locations, and construct-preserving parse results.
Exact CPython SyntaxError, SyntaxWarning, incomplete-input, invalid_* rule ordering, and location behavior remains future work tied to the diagnostics profile.

known_gaps: The current K parser does not natively implement the full Python PEG grammar.
The adapter relies on CPython ast.parse and therefore inherits CPython parser acceptance, rejection, normalization, and AST-shape decisions for inputs it can lower.
The current adapter supports only a subset of AST nodes and does not yet preserve every concrete syntax distinction from Grammar/python.gram.
The full invalid_* second-pass parser diagnostics, source spans, token stream, soft keyword decisions, and exact incomplete-input behavior are not modeled.
Completion requires either a native K parser or a documented verified parser frontend that preserves every official construct needed by the semantics.
